Refs #18145. **Does not close it** — 5 `Global.scss` files stay baselined pending #18232.

One line: the baseline `reason` for the `theme-neo-{light,dark}/dialog/Base.scss` exemption.

## Why

I set out to spend the exemption — move the nested selector into `src/` and let each theme value the tokens flat. I built it and it does not hold. The exemption is right; the **recorded reason was wrong about why**, in a way that would let the next attempt repeat mine.

The structural rule is `.neo-dialog.neo-panel .neo-header-toolbar .neo-button` — **(0,4,0)**, not (0,3,0). It outweighs **13** of the 16 `background-color` states a header button can win, so spending the exemption means enumerating all 13 as tokens — which converts an open extension point into a closed enumeration: a future button variant would silently stop applying inside dialog headers, with nothing failing.

The other **3** (ghost/secondary/tertiary `:active`) are not a specificity question — they declare `!important` (`resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:205,258,317`) and keep winning regardless. They need no token.

**The trap:** moving the base declaration alone looks correct and leaves every per-file emitted-CSS diff clean, because the classic-theme regression is a cascade outcome no single file shows.

Full measurement lives on #18145 — deliberately not restated here or in the JSON.

## Evidence

`node buildScripts/util/check-theme-value-files.mjs` → exit 0, `5 pending, 2 exempt` (unchanged).

## Review history

The first two versions of this reason were both wrong, both caught by @neo-gpt with exact-head Chromium probes: v1 claimed all 16 were specificity-reachable; v2 overshot the other way, claiming a move would need to reproduce an `!important` flag. It would not. This is v3.

The reason string was also **1788 characters** against a house idiom of 65–106 in that file — now 209, stating the finding and linking the measurement.
